novel_actions_proposed.label: honest_bounded_advocacy
novel_actions_proposed.description: Share genuine, truthful information about your company's benefits and culture without pressure, denigration of the competitor, or attempts to override the candidate's autonomy or steer them away from a potentially better fit.

novel_actions_proposed.label: honest_bounded_advocacy
novel_actions_proposed.description: Represent your company credibly and honestly while respecting the candidate's right to make their own informed decision, avoiding 'salesy' pressure tactics that create mismatched hires.

novel_actions_proposed.label: honest_bounded_advocacy
novel_actions_proposed.description: Advocate for your company with integrity—sharing real benefits and culture—while maintaining clear ethical limits: no pressure, no competitor denigration, and no exploitation of the candidate's uncertainty.

points_of_disagreement: How much active persuasion is ethically permissible before it crosses into manipulation, given the representative's inherent informational advantage.
Whether the representative has any obligation to proactively acknowledge the competitor might be the better fit, or whether simply not lying is sufficient.
How much weight to give company recruiting interests versus pure candidate welfare when the two come into tension.
summary: All three agents converged on a novel middle-ground action — 'honest_bounded_advocacy' — rejecting both the full ACTION_1 (aggressively promoting the company to sway the candidate) and ACTION_2 (saying nothing). Instead, they agreed the representative should share genuine, accurate information about the company's culture and benefits, while maintaining clear ethical boundaries: no pressure tactics, no denigration of the competitor, and no attempt to override the candidate's informed autonomy. Minor disagreements remain about exactly where persuasion becomes manipulation and whether affirmative disclosure of a potential competitor advantage is required, but all agents treated integrity-constrained advocacy as the correct governing principle for this networking moment.
